hooks.name: platform-reader
hooks.reason: Builds the membership and cluster-state reader of a deployed Slurm Platform from its Connection: plain REST against slurmrestd at the pinned API version.

hooks.name: platform-credential
hooks.reason: Turns the Slurm credential role's result into the slurmrestd read Integration, pinning the API version the controller reported; a deployment without slurmrestd records none.

hooks.name: platform
hooks.reason: Converts between the Platform spec and the Slurm deploy request (members as nodeAssignments, node groups and partitions in the slurm setting), plans the groups' partitions and Features, and classifies a spec change per desired-state-model §5.2, blocking control-plane changes swallow does not scale.

validations.title: Slurm acceptance
validations.description: Checks that a step runs on every node, that jobs share a node, that containers run and see only their GPUs, that MPI launches through PMIx, that Slurm hands out exactly the GPUs a job asks for, and that a HIP kernel runs on them in a container. It reads the nodes and features from the cluster and runs short jobs, so it competes with the cluster's workload. Every Slurm deployment runs it as its gate on the nodes the deployment adds; there, GPU nodes that fail are drained.

gpuServers.title: GPU Servers
gpuServers.description: Servers that must offer GPU GRES. Default: none beyond the nodes whose GRES names GPUs.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: Servers the node checks run on (a deployment's gate names the nodes it adds). Default: every compute node.

containerImage.title: Container image
containerImage.description: ROCm image the container GPU check builds and runs its HIP probe in; each GPU node pulls it from its registry when missing. Default: none, which skips the check.

containerRuntime.title: Container runtime
containerRuntime.description: docker-ce or podman: what the container GPU check runs the image with. Default: none, which skips it.

checks.title: Step on every node
checks.description: One task runs on every node the run checks at once, and every one of them is a node.

checks.title: Jobs share a node
checks.description: Two one-CPU jobs without a memory request run on one node together, unless the partition hands out whole nodes.

checks.title: Native OCI containers
checks.description: A native OCI container step runs rootless and sees exactly one GPU when it asks for one.

checks.title: MPI with PMIx
checks.description: srun --mpi=pmix_v5 launches ranks on one node, across nodes, and in containers, and a failing rank fails its step.

checks.title: GPU GRES
checks.description: Every GPU node offers GPU GRES, and jobs get exactly the GPUs they ask for: none without a request, one with one, and every GPU for the whole node (the host HIP probe only records).

checks.title: GPUs in a container
checks.description: On every GPU node, a HIP probe built with hipcc inside AMD's ROCm image runs a kernel on exactly the GPUs a job is given, in the Platform's container runtime. Skipped, with the reason, when the node cannot pull the image or the Platform has no container runtime; a probe that fails to build or run fails.

slurm_drain_timeout.remediation: Jobs still run on a node that is leaving the Platform. Wait for them, raise the removal's drainTimeoutSeconds, or set force to end them, then retry.

slurm_node_unreachable.remediation: A node leaving the Platform cannot be reached, so it cannot be cleaned. Bring it back and retry, or set force on its removal to finish without cleaning it (the cluster already no longer uses it).

slurm_drain_failed.remediation: slurmctld refused to drain a leaving node; check that the node is known to the cluster (scontrol show node) and the controller is up, then retry.

slurm_unmount_busy.remediation: A process on the leaving node still uses the shared workload filesystem. Stop it (fuser -vm <mount path>) and retry.

amd_smi_missing.remediation: The GPU node has no amd-smi. The image must ship the AMD SMI library and its CLI with the amdgpu driver.

amd_smi_unhealthy.remediation: AMD SMI lists fewer GPUs than KFD, or reports uncorrectable ECC errors. Check the GPUs (amd-smi list, amd-smi metric --ecc) and the driver; replace or reset the faulty GPU, then retry.
